Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Government to provide funding to Ghana EXIM Bank to finance NADKANSCO’s year-round cashew purchases – Mahama Source : Albert Kuzor 16 November 2026 5:40pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
President John Dramani Mahama has announced plans to provide additional funding to the Ghana Export-Import Bank (Ghana EXIM Bank) to enable it to finance NADKANSCO Cashew Processing Limited's purchase of raw cashew nuts throughout the year.
He said the intervention was intended to address working capital challenges facing the factory and ensure it secures enough raw materials to sustain production beyond the cashew harvesting season.
Speaking at the commissioning of the EXIM Bank-funded NADKANSCO factory in Techiman on Monday, November 16, 2026, President Mahama said the government would make funds available to Ghana EXIM Bank to lend to the company.
He explained that although the bank had financed the factory's capital expenditure, including machinery and equipment, additional resources were required to purchase sufficient quantities of raw cashew nuts.
“Exim has financed the capital expenditure, the machines and everything. And in addition, they are giving money for working capital. But if you look at the volume of cashew that we produce, you are going to need much more than $100 million to purchase enough cashew to keep this factory running all year round,” he said.
President Mahama noted that the working capital currently available to the company would sustain operations for only about 60 to 80 days.
He said government did not want the factory to operate for a few months and shut down until the next harvesting season, particularly given the employment opportunities it provides.
“We don't want a factory that will run for 80 days, shut down for the rest of the year, until the next cashew season. NADKANSCO should be able to buy enough cashew and preserve it so that the young people here can have work all the year round,” he said.
The President said the additional financing would form part of government's broader investment in the agribusiness and tree crops sectors under its new economy agenda.
“So as part of the new economy, like I said, we are devoting money for agribusiness. And in agribusiness, the tree crops sector is included. And so cashew is a part of the new economy,” he said.
He added: “We will lend money to Ghana EXIM to on-lend to NADKANSCO so that NADKANSCO can acquire enough cashew nuts to process throughout the year.”
President Mahama also announced plans to restrict raw cashew exports during the first three months of the harvesting season to give local processors priority in purchasing the commodity.
Government, he said, would further introduce a levy on exported raw cashew nuts, with the proceeds channelled into a fund to support local processing companies.
The measures are intended to ensure that more of Ghana's cashew production is processed locally, creating jobs and retaining greater economic value within the country.
